verdict.rationale: Superpowers ships its own meta-skill, writing-skills, which teaches the agent to author and test new skills through a TDD loop: pressure-scenario tests, baseline failure, writing the SKILL.md, then refactoring. A hands-on probe shows skills are plain markdown folders that can be installed one at a time. The packaging and distribution half of the story is thin: the evidence names the cross-runtime skills directory but does not document how an agent packages or publishes a newly authored skill. missing for 10: documented end-to-end packaging/publishing steps for a new skill (manifest, marketplace or plugin submission), independent hands-on corroboration of an agent authoring a new skill via writing-skills.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can author and package a new skill end to end by following the project's own spec, template, or meta-skill

citations.quote: You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).
The writing-skills module teaches you to author and test new skills
Writing skills IS Test-Driven Development applied to process documentation.
Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all also recognize `~/.agents/skills/` as a cross-runtime alias.
Skills are plain, selectively-installable markdown folders.
